children: post-halving cycles have historically entered a phase of sustained price strength near the 1,000-day mark.

Coin Metrics data covering the 2012, 2016, and 2020 cycles show that, when measured as a multiple of each cycle’s halving-day price, bitcoin recorded its strongest gains in the period that followed day 1,000. In each prior instance, price action had appeared subdued or under pressure in the weeks immediately before that threshold, only to reverse higher afterward.

The current cycle is approaching the same calendar window, with day 1,000 now 53 days away. As of Tuesday afternoon, bitcoin is trading near $59,656, lower by -2.5% on the session. The cryptocurrency remains approximately 52.7% below its all-time high of $126,272, set on October 6, 2025—just over one year ago.

The alignment of the present timeline with prior cycle behavior has drawn renewed attention from market participants tracking longer-term bitcoin structure. While the historical pattern has been consistent across previous halvings, price action continues to be shaped by macroeconomic conditions, liquidity trends, and institutional positioning. Whether the current cycle follows the same post-day 1,000 trajectory remains an open question that will be tested in the weeks ahead.

title: Bitcoin is 53% off its peak, with the historic cycle clock nearly done
